text: Let’s talk numbers. Biryani that was once $8 went to $10 then $16. A half-tray of chicken biryani used to cost $40 then $45 then $50. But when Ramadan came around—a sacred time when Muslims focus on prayer and devotion—the price quietly jumped to $60. That’s right. The very community that helped build this business was rewarded with price gouging during their holiest month. A true Muslim businessman would honor his customers especially during Ramadan. If anything he would keep prices stable (or even lower them) because he knows he will make more on volume. But greed has a way of clouding judgment.
